name: Gilgamesh flood narrative from Nineveh
description: A cuneiform tablet preserved in Ashurbanipal’s library records a flood episode within the Epic of Gilgamesh.

impact.note: A single library tablet copying an older epic; its only known consequence is the modern recovery of Gilgamesh that leaned on Nineveh copies.

date.label: 7th century BCE
date.basis: The British Museum dates the tablet to the seventh century BCE.

events.statement: A tablet from Ashurbanipal’s library preserves the flood episode of Gilgamesh.
events.scope: The surviving tablet is a late witness to a much older literary tradition; this does not date its composition or represent the whole epic.
events.caveats: The surviving tablet is a late witness to a much older literary tradition; this does not date its composition or represent the whole epic.

evidence.supports: A tablet from Ashurbanipal’s library preserves the flood episode of Gilgamesh.

earliest_record.rationale: The British Museum dates the tablet to the seventh century BCE. Earliest supported episode established here, not a claim of world priority.
